solution.summary: The bid is a 15-month research and proof-of-concept engagement for MHTC/MoDOT, run by MoDOT's Research Unit, that determines whether AI/ML can produce a usable first draft of a legal land description (LLD) for Right of Way staff to review and edit. We deliver a literature review of other state DOTs' AI/ML use in right of way, a named and IS-approved LLD generation program, a demonstration of draft LLDs across a variety of property types, a trained ROW user base with a user manual, and the draft and final reports, research summary and staff presentation. The shape is mostly build-and-configure on a small, MoDOT-compliant web application plus research and advisory work; nothing is procured on MoDOT's behalf and no licensing burden is placed on MoDOT. Delivery runs in four phases: mobilisation and planning (kick-off, work plan, Data Management Plan, program naming and IS approval), research and baseline (literature review, EPG 236.4.6.2 and MHTC parameter capture), build and demonstrate (iterative LLD generation with MoDOT feedback, 4/25/2025 demonstration), then training, reporting and close-out (manual and training by 7/25/2025, interim presentation 9/15/2025, drafts 11/3/2025, finals 1/1/2026, final invoice 2/2/2026). The team is a principal investigator-led research group with a land-surveying/ROW subject-matter expert, an AI/ML engineer, a .NET web developer, a technical writer/trainer and a contract-compliance lead, all coordinated with the Construction and Materials Division. Everything is priced inside the $175,000 not-to-exceed cap on the Section (4) Price Page line items, and the bid is filed and every question channelled through MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by the RFP's stated deadlines.

components.title: Bid administration, submission and clarification discipline
components.description: We run the proposal itself as a controlled deliverable: the combined PDF is filed to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov before the RFP's stated proposal deadline, and we treat time as of the essence, holding internal sign-off and file-assembly dates ahead of the deadline so no late or partial filing is possible. Every question or comment on the RFP is sent only to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by the date and time listed in Section 1E, and no member of the bid team contacts MoDOT employees by any other method, since doing so is cause for disqualification. We log each question, the date sent and MoDOT's posted response, and we build the proposal on the assumption that MoDOT's written responses and clarifications govern. This component also carries the post-award close-out discipline: the final invoice is submitted and the contract closed on 2/2/2026, with all billing completed against the 1/1/2026 final deliverables so nothing is left outstanding at contract end.

claims.text: Proposals are due by 10 a.m. Central on August 21, 2024 to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov, with receipt acknowledged by noon the same day.
All questions and comments must go only to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by 4 p.m. Central on July 17, 2024.
The final invoice is due and the contract ends on 2/2/2026.

components.title: Mobilisation, work plan and governance
components.description: We facilitate the kick-off meeting with MoDOT on 11/15/2024 to review the work plan, scope and schedule and to agree a protocol for regular communication and coordination with the Research Unit and Construction and Materials Division. We finalise a work plan that details implementation of every project task together with the resources and schedule needed to carry them out, and that expressly recognises MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve work plans. The plan is built to the 15-month contract period and to the fixed milestone calendar, and we consult MHTC's designated representative (MoDOT Research Director Jen Harper or her delegate) on any concern about administration of the services, with a standing monthly check-in for that purpose. We fully coordinate our activities with the Construction and Materials Division and keep advice and information on matters covered by the Agreement available to that Division throughout the term.

claims.text: MoDOT's Research Director, Jen Harper, is MHTC's designated representative for administering the agreement and may delegate authority.
The contract period is 15 months, estimated to start 11/1/2024 and end 2/2/2026.

components.title: Reporting, meetings and schedule control
components.description: We run a single reporting calendar that satisfies every cadence the RFP sets: monthly e-mail and phone updates to MoDOT contacts on progress, quarterly written updates on work accomplished submitted on or before the last working day of March, June, September and December, and quarterly status meetings (in person or online) reviewing the previous period and the anticipated next period. We produce written minutes for the kick-off meeting and for every quarterly status meeting and circulate them for MoDOT confirmation. We schedule the interim presentation near the project mid-point, and no later than 9/15/2025, to update MoDOT on progress and project direction. All meetings and events are scheduled between 7:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. Central time, and the schedule is tracked against the fixed milestone dates with early warning to MoDOT of any slippage.

claims.text: MoDOT's fiscal year runs July 1 to June 30, which drives the quarterly reporting cycle submitted to FHWA.

components.title: Data Management Plan and data handling
components.description: We deliver a Data Management Plan to MoDOT within two weeks of the kick-off meeting, and in any event by the 12/4/2024 milestone, describing the anticipated formats of our data and related files. The DMP commits us to platform-independent, non-proprietary formats (for example plain-text/CSV, GeoJSON and PDF/A) so the data retains maximum future utility for MoDOT, and it sets out storage, versioning, retention and hand-back of the working papers and records we must maintain. It also records our PII position: no personally identifiable information is stored in any database table without a specific business need, and any PII that is stored is submitted for IS Cyber Security Team approval before the table is created.

claims.text: The Data Management Plan is due within two weeks after the kick-off meeting, and the milestone table fixes 12/4/2024.

components.title: Literature review of state DOT AI/ML practice
components.description: We conduct a thorough literature search and review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right-of-way purposes, covering published research, DOT technical reports, peer-exchange material and vendor case studies, and we deliver it as a structured report with a comparison matrix of use cases, methods, results and lessons learned. The review is scoped with MoDOT at kick-off so that the states, period and ROW use cases covered match what the Research Unit and Right of Way staff need, and its findings feed directly into the design of the LLD generation approach and the final report.

components.title: LLD generation program: naming, IS approval and compliance
components.description: Before any proof-of-concept work begins we name the program we will use to develop the LLDs and submit it, with version, licensing, hosting and security information, for MoDOT Information Systems approval; no Task 3c work starts until that approval is in hand. The application is built on a currently supported .NET 6.0 or above release (falling back to .NET Framework 4.8 or above only if a specific need is shown), using MVC, Razor Pages or Web API, and written in the approved languages C#, JavaScript, CSS, HTML and Python, with Python confined to ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless the IS Best Practices Review Team approves larger use. It is a web-based browser application requiring no client-side software beyond a modern browser (no Java Applets, no Silverlight), tested against the latest IS-approved browsers, and it meets the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard (Section 508 as amended and WCAG) including WCAG 2.1 AA. It runs on Oracle 19C for on-premise deployment, with any SQL Server option used only where MoDOT IS Data Service Management approves it, and library dependencies are reviewed and updated annually. We use no third-party tool or software that places a licensing responsibility on MoDOT without prior review and approval by the IS Best Practices Review Team and IS management, and we use no text, diagrams, photographs, audio, multimedia, source code, scripts or graphics from another author's web pages unless the author permits free copying or arrangements are made with the author. Vendor logos and branding are suppressed wherever a supported, licensed option exists to remove them.

claims.text: MoDOT Information Systems must approve the named LLD development program before Task 3c can proceed.

components.title: EPG-compliant LLD drafting engine and MHTC parameter capture
components.description: We build the drafting engine that turns MHTC parameters into a first-draft legal land description for MoDOT Right of Way staff to review and edit. The engine encodes the drafting rules the RFP requires: descriptions are produced in metes and bounds form, and where a property is acquired in its entirety the description is reproduced exactly as it appears on the last deed of record for that property. Output is generated to meet MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide Section 236.4.6.2, and every draft is routed for professional land surveyor review against the right of way plans before any deed is presented to a grantor. We capture the MHTC parameters and the EPG rules in a documented parameter and rules specification agreed with MoDOT at kick-off, so the drafting logic is auditable and can be tuned as feedback arrives.

claims.text: Descriptions prepared for MHTC must meet EPG Section 236.4.6.2 and be reviewed by a professional land surveyor against the right of way plans before a deed is presented to the grantor.

components.title: Proof of concept, demonstration and feedback loop
components.description: We run the proof of concept on a set of MoDOT-supplied example LLDs and a variety of property types agreed at kick-off, generating draft LLDs and capturing MoDOT's review comments as structured improvement feedback. On 4/25/2025 we present how the AI/ML creates draft LLDs and how MoDOT feedback is incorporated for improvement, demonstrating the AI writing a legal land description live against the agreed property set. We then adjust the tool on the basis of that feedback before training, and we demonstrate draft LLD generation across the variety of properties required, with each round's outputs and changes recorded so MoDOT can see the improvement trajectory.

claims.text: MoDOT supplies example LLDs on 12/20/2024 for the proof of concept.

components.title: Training, user manual and ROW staff enablement
components.description: After the tool adjustments, and by 7/25/2025, we deliver a written user manual and train MoDOT Right of Way staff on the tool. The manual is a standalone reference document covering the parameter inputs, how to run a draft, how to review and edit the output, and the surveyor review step, delivered in an accessible, platform-independent format and updated once more before the final submission. Training is delivered in sessions sized and formatted to the audience MoDOT confirms at kick-off, with recorded sessions and the manual left with MoDOT so new staff can be onboarded after the contract ends.

components.title: Reports, research summary and staff presentation
components.description: We prepare the draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary with all accompanying documentation identified as beneficial during the study, due 11/3/2025, and the final report, research summary, presentation and user manual due 1/1/2026, roughly a month before contract end so all billing can be completed. The research summary is a 1-2 page statement of project objectives, findings and conclusions, and the presentation summarises the significant details of the project for MoDOT staff. Reports follow the MoDOT Publication Guidelines and the research summary template, and the final report carries a completed Technical Report Documentation page.

claims.text: The draft final report, summary report and user manual are due 11/3/2025 and the final versions 1/1/2026, with the contract ending 2/2/2026.

components.title: Pricing, contract and compliance obligations
components.description: We price the whole scope of work at a total not to exceed $175,000 and submit a proposed cost estimate covering all services in the Scope of Work on Section (4), the Price Page, broken out into Salaries, Benefits, Operating Expense, Facilities and Administration (F&A) Cost, Miscellaneous and Total, with Miscellaneous costs itemised on an additional sheet where needed; we agree to provide the services at the fees quoted under the terms of the RFP. We accept that the award incorporates the contract provisions specified in the RFP and is subject to a post-award negotiated contract, and that MHTC may cancel the award and select another Offeror if terms cannot be agreed; we accept that written clarifications issued by MHTC govern over conflicting requirements, and that any change to the Agreement requires a formal amendment signed by both authorised representatives. We will not release any material or report to the public without MHTC's representative's prior consent, will not assign, delegate or novate any interest without prior written consent, and will not disclose confidential factual matters supplied by MHTC except as required by statute, ordinance or court order or as authorised by MHTC's representative, notifying MHTC immediately of any such request. All documents, reports, exhibits and deliverables we produce at MHTC's direction, and all information MHTC supplies, remain MHTC property, and we maintain all working papers and records and make them available at no charge to MHTC and the Missouri State Auditor at all reasonable times during the term and for three years from final payment. We remain ultimately responsible and liable to MHTC for the complete, accurate and professional quality and performance of the services regardless of any subcontractor or supplier, and we flow the Section (3) paragraph I provisions into every subcontract and take such action with respect to any subcontract as the Commission may direct, including sanctions for noncompliance. We comply with Missouri Executive Order 07-13, certify by signature that every employee assigned is eligible and authorised to work in the United States, submit the Exhibit A sworn affidavit of E-Verify enrolment and no unauthorised alien employment, and submit the Exhibit B affidavit of lawful presence where the Offeror is a sole proprietorship or partnership. We will provide General Liability and Automobile Liability insurance of at least $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence and a Missouri workers' compensation policy, and can evidence certificates before signing. We pursue 10% MBE and 5% WBE participation through subcontracting and direct hiring of minorities and women, while remaining fully liable for subcontractor performance.

claims.text: Services are capped at a not-to-exceed amount of $175,000.
Offerors may be asked before signing to provide insurance of at least $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence plus Missouri workers' compensation.

assumptions.text: The 8/21/2024 10 a.m. Central proposal deadline is treated as fixed and protected, and the November 1, 2024 start with the milestone dates through 2/2/2026 is treated as the baseline schedule, with any re-baselining at the 11/15/2024 kick-off limited to internal task sequencing rather than the fixed deliverable dates.
The 7/17/2024 4 p.m. Central date is treated as the deadline for submitting questions and comments on the RFP, and no question is raised after it.
The Data Management Plan is delivered by the earlier of the two stated dates, i.e. within two weeks of the 11/15/2024 kick-off, which also satisfies the 12/4/2024 milestone.
The interim presentation is scheduled at the project mid-point and in any event no later than 9/15/2025, so the 9/15/2025 date governs if the two conflict.

The $175,000 cap is an all-inclusive ceiling covering every task in the Scope of Work, including training, reporting and travel, and the cost estimate is priced for the full 15-month term rather than per year.

The MHTC parameters and the content of EPG Section 236.4.6.2 are assumed to be obtainable from MoDOT at kick-off and captured in a written parameter and rules specification agreed with the Research Unit before build begins.

The proof of concept is assumed to cover a modest set of property types (roughly 10-20 example properties) drawn from the MoDOT-supplied example LLDs, with the demonstration delivered live with recorded backup.

Training is assumed to be delivered as a small number of virtual or on-site sessions for the MoDOT Right of Way review group, with a standalone PDF user manual, sized within the fixed price rather than priced per trainee.

The literature review is assumed to be delivered as a written report with a comparison matrix covering other state DOTs' AI/ML right-of-way uses over roughly the last decade, since the RFP sets no narrower scope.

The LLD generation program is assumed to be a MoDOT-hosted web application on Oracle 19C built in .NET 6.0 or above, with no third-party component that creates a licensing obligation for MoDOT, so no BRPT licensing review is triggered.
The insurance limits are treated as binding contract requirements to be evidenced by certificate before signing rather than with the proposal.
The 10% MBE and 5% WBE goals are treated as aspirational participation targets we will document and report, not as a pass/fail condition of the proposal.

The Publication Guidelines, research summary template, Price Page, Proposal Submission Form and Standard Research Agreement are assumed to be the versions currently posted at https://www.modot.org/information-researchers and are incorporated as the governing formats.

The Section (3) paragraph I subcontract provisions and the Executive Order 07-13 obligations are assumed to be the standard MoDOT flow-down terms, which we accept and pass through to subcontractors without negotiation.

Confidential factual matters are assumed to be marked as confidential by MHTC at the time of supply, with notification of any third-party request made to MHTC's representative within one business day.
